Vote choice and issue distances in the 1987 British general election (Glasgow 2001)

Source: R/data.R
bes1987.Rd

Respondents of the 1987 British General Election Study who voted Conservative, Labour or Alliance, with their distance to each party on seven issues and their social and economic characteristics (Glasgow 2001, following Alvarez, Nagler and Bowler 2000). One row per respondent and party (the long layout); the classic example of the IIA debate in political science and of the mixed logit as its remedy.

Usage

data(bes1987)

Format

A data frame with 6,393 rows (2,131 respondents times 3 parties) and 26 variables:

id

Respondent identifier.

party

Factor: conservative, labour, alliance.

chosen

1 for the party voted for.

defense, phillips, taxation, nationalization, redistribution, crime, welfare

Distance between the respondent and the party on the issue: the absolute difference between the respondent's self-placement and the party's mean placement by all respondents, on 11-point scales (defense: nuclear weapons; phillips: inflation versus unemployment; crime: civil rights versus fighting crime).

south, midlands, north, wales, scotland

Region of residence.

union

1 if a member of a trade union or staff association.

public

1 if employed in the public sector.

working_class

1 if in a working-class (manual, personal service or agricultural) occupation.

female

1 if female.

age

Age in years divided by 10.

homeowner

1 if the household owns its residence.

income

Family income, 1 to 12.

education

Age at the end of continuous full-time education, divided by 10.

inflation, taxes, unemployment

Perceived change since the 1983 election in prices, taxes and unemployment, 1 (increased a lot) to 5 (fallen a lot).

Source

Glasgow, G. (2001). Mixed logit models for multiparty elections. Political Analysis, 9, 116-136. Data: Heath, A., Jowell, R. and Curtice, J.K. British General Election Study, 1987: Cross-Section Survey. UK Data Service, SN 2568. doi:10.5255/UKDA-SN-2568-1

Provenance and terms

From the replication archive of Glasgow (2001) at the Harvard Dataverse (doi:10.7910/DVN/PCPVWB , version 1.0, released under CC0 1.0): the file glasgow.data.asc of glasgow.web.zip (md5 ab0c27430d5b281eed1859ebb88b64bc), its 39 columns read in the order of the archive's GAUSS program. The survey is the British General Election Study, 1987: Cross-Section Survey (Heath, Jowell and Curtice; UK Data Service SN 2568, doi:10.5255/UKDA-SN-2568-1 ), which the UK Data Service distributes under the Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 licence; use of these data should cite it. The rebuilding script is data-raw/make_examples.R of the development repository. The multinomial logit of the paper's Appendix A, Table C (log-likelihood -1477.56) reproduces.

See also

Other datasets: afghan_leaders, bes2010, cabinets, defection, fluvax, pa2006, pres2004, sanctions

Examples

data(bes1987)
f <- chosen ~ defense + phillips + taxation + nationalization + redistribution + crime + welfare |
  south + midlands + north + wales + scotland + union + public + working_class + female + age +
  homeowner + income + education + inflation + taxes + unemployment
m <- mnl(f, data = bes1987, id = "id", alt = "party", ref = "alliance")
m$loglik                                # Appendix A, Table C: -1477.56
#> [1] -1477.557
# \donttest{
iia_tests(m, seed = 1)
#> Tests of IIA / misspecification of the multinomial logit 
#>                                            test  alternative statistic df
#>                   Hausman-McFadden (difference) conservative    59.860 24
#>                   Hausman-McFadden (difference)       labour   -42.232 24
#>                   Hausman-McFadden (difference)     alliance   108.317 24
#>                        Hausman-McFadden (joint) conservative    25.395 24
#>                        Hausman-McFadden (joint)       labour    30.454 24
#>                        Hausman-McFadden (joint)     alliance    34.068 24
#>                Small-Hsiao (median over splits) conservative    21.212 24
#>                Small-Hsiao (median over splits)       labour    25.852 24
#>                Small-Hsiao (median over splits)     alliance    29.999 24
#>                 Fok-Paap CL Hausman (Q1, joint)                 67.563 41
#>  Fok-Paap GMM overidentification (Q2, two-step)                 44.544 31
#>   p.value   psd share_separated
#>  6.68e-05  TRUE              NA
#>   1.00000 FALSE              NA

#> psd = FALSE: the covariance difference was not positive semi-definite for that row. A negative statistic is no evidence against the model (p-value 1); a positive one from a variance-difference form is unreliable (see the test's help).
